title: VA Home Loan Guaranty Liquidation, Guaranty Claims and the Home Loan Guaranty Debt
content:
When a defaulted loan backed by the VA Home Loan Guaranty is liquidated by foreclosure, compromise sale or deed in lieu, VA pays the holder a guaranty claim no larger than the guaranty.

## Consequences of the claim

1. The claim paid creates a Home Loan Guaranty Debt for the veteran, unless the veteran was released from liability on an approved assumption.
2. A borrower completing a compromise sale or deed in lieu may receive up to the program's maximum relocation assistance.
3. Any unpaid partial claim is repaid from sale proceeds before the veteran receives anything.

## Decision table

| Released from liability on an approved assumption | Guaranty claim paid on liquidation | Home Loan Guaranty Debt created for the veteran |
|---|---|---|
| No | Yes | Yes |
| Yes | Yes | No |

| Way the loan was liquidated | Relocation assistance available to the borrower |
|---|---|
| Compromise sale | Up to the program maximum |
| Deed in lieu | Up to the program maximum |

## Worked example (hypothetical)

Hypothetical inputs: a guaranty of 60,000.00 dollars on the loan; the holder's loss on liquidation would support a claim of 75,000.00 dollars; the veteran was not released from liability.

The claim paid is no larger than the guaranty, so it is at most 60,000.00 dollars, and the claim paid creates a Home Loan Guaranty Debt for the veteran. On the same facts with a release of liability on an approved assumption, the claim would create no debt for the veteran.

## Order of proceeds

From the proceeds of a sale, any unpaid partial claim is repaid first; the veteran receives nothing before it is repaid.
